basil.store: Stems in a glass of water at room temperature: the fridge blackens it.
basil.preserve: Make pesto and freeze it in ice-cube trays.

parsley.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a week.
parsley.preserve: Chop and freeze, or blitz into a green sauce.
parsley.use: By the handful: tabbouleh, salsa verde, over everything.

coriander.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a few days.
coriander.preserve: Freeze chopped in oil; save the seeds when it bolts.
coriander.use: Leaves in curries and salsas; the seeds ground for spice.

chives.store: Snip as you need them; they wilt fast once cut.
chives.use: Over eggs, potatoes and soured cream; the flowers in salads.

mint.store: Stems in water in the fridge for a week.
mint.preserve: Make mint sauce, or dry the leaves for tea.
mint.use: With peas and new potatoes, or fresh mint tea.

rosemary.store: Pick as needed all year; it keeps a week in the fridge.

thyme.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
thyme.preserve: Dries well: hang small bunches somewhere airy.
thyme.use: In stews, with mushrooms, and on roast chicken.

sage.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
sage.preserve: Dry the leaves, or fry them crisp and keep in a jar for a few days.
sage.use: Fried in butter with squash or pasta.

dill.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
dill.preserve: Freeze chopped; save the seeds for pickling.

oregano.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
oregano.preserve: Dries better than almost any herb.

fennel.store: Fronds in water in the fridge for a few days.
fennel.preserve: Dry the seeds when they turn brown.
fennel.use: Fronds with fish; seeds in bread and sausages.

lemon-balm.store: Stems in water for a few days.
lemon-balm.use: Fresh in tea, or with fruit.

bay.preserve: Dry the leaves flat for a fortnight.
bay.use: In stocks, stews and rice pudding.

tarragon.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
tarragon.preserve: Keep sprigs in white wine vinegar.

sorrel.store: In a bag in the fridge for a day or two.
sorrel.preserve: Cook to a purée and freeze.
sorrel.use: Lemony leaves in salads, or a sauce for fish.

lovage.store: In the fridge for a few days.
lovage.use: A little goes a long way: like celery, in soups and stocks.

horseradish.store: Lift roots as needed, or keep in damp sand.
horseradish.preserve: Grate into vinegar, or make horseradish sauce.
horseradish.use: Grated fresh with roast beef or smoked fish. Grate it by an open window.

salad-burnet.store: Pick as needed: it wilts fast.
salad-burnet.use: Cucumber-flavoured leaves in salads and drinks.

chervil.store: In a bag in the fridge for a couple of days.
chervil.use: Gently aniseed: with eggs and fish.

chamomile.store: Dry the flowers soon after picking.
chamomile.preserve: Dried in a jar for a year.

marjoram.store: Pick as needed; a week in the fridge.
marjoram.use: Gentler than oregano: with tomatoes and lamb.

winter-savory.store: Pick as needed, even in winter.

hyssop.use: A little, minty and bitter, with fatty meat or in tea.

lemon-verbena.preserve: Dry the leaves: they keep their scent.
lemon-verbena.use: Tea, or steeped in cream for ice cream.

lemongrass.store: Stalks in the fridge for a couple of weeks.
lemongrass.use: Bruised into curries, soups and tea.

shiso.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.

holy-basil.store: Stems in a glass of water on the side, not the fridge.
holy-basil.use: In Thai stir-fries, or steeped for tea.

lemon-basil.store: Stems in water on the side for a day or two.
lemon-basil.preserve: Blend with oil and freeze in an ice tray.
lemon-basil.use: Torn over fish, salads and fruit.

peppermint.store: Stems in a glass of water, or wrapped in the fridge.
peppermint.use: Fresh mint tea; with chocolate puddings.

apple-mint.store: Stems in a glass of water for a few days.
apple-mint.preserve: Dry for tea, or chop into ice cubes.
apple-mint.use: With new potatoes, peas and fruit salads.

water-mint.store: Stems in a glass of water for a day or two.
water-mint.use: Strong and peppery: in tea, or sparingly in sauces.

lemon-thyme.store: Sprigs in the fridge for a week.
lemon-thyme.use: With chicken, fish and lemony puddings.

creeping-thyme.store: Sprigs in the fridge for a week.

sweet-cicely.store: In the fridge for a few days.
sweet-cicely.use: Leaves cooked with rhubarb or gooseberries; green seeds nibbled.

angelica.store: Stems in the fridge for a few days.
angelica.preserve: Candy the young stems in syrup.
angelica.use: Candied for cakes, or a stem cooked with rhubarb.

caraway.store: Dry seeds in a jar for a year.
caraway.preserve: Hang the heads in a paper bag to catch the seeds.
caraway.use: In rye bread, cabbage and seed cake; young leaves in salad.

fenugreek.store: Leaves in the fridge for a couple of days; seeds in a jar.
fenugreek.use: Leaves in curries and flatbreads; seeds toasted and ground.

vietnamese-coriander.store: Stems in a glass of water for a few days.
vietnamese-coriander.use: In laksa, noodle salads and summer rolls.

mitsuba.store: In the fridge for a few days.
mitsuba.use: In clear soups, egg dishes and salads: like celery and parsley together.

culantro.store: Wrapped in damp paper in the fridge for a week.
culantro.use: In Caribbean and South East Asian cooking, added near the end.

stevia.store: Dry leaves in a jar for a year.
stevia.use: A leaf or two in tea, or a pinch of dried leaf to sweeten fruit.

roman-chamomile.store: Dried flowers in a jar for a year.

sweet-woodruff.store: Wilted sprigs keep their scent for weeks, dried.
sweet-woodruff.use: A wilted sprig steeped in white wine or cream: it smells of new hay.

wild-garlic.store: In a bag in the fridge for a few days.
wild-garlic.use: In pesto, soups and scrambled eggs; the flowers over salads.

bergamot.store: Dried leaves in a jar for a year.
bergamot.use: Steeped for tea; the petals over salads.

anise-hyssop.use: Liquorice-scented tea, or the flowers on cakes.

cutting-celery.store: In the fridge for a week.
cutting-celery.preserve: Dry or freeze the chopped leaves.
cutting-celery.use: In stocks, soups and stews, as celery.

rock-samphire.store: In the fridge for a few days.
rock-samphire.preserve: Pickle it in vinegar, as was traditional.
rock-samphire.use: Pickled, or blanched and served with fish.

red-veined-sorrel.store: In a bag in the fridge for a couple of days.
red-veined-sorrel.use: Small leaves in salads, for colour and a sharp edge.

french-sorrel.store: In a bag in the fridge for a couple of days.
french-sorrel.preserve: Cook into a sauce and freeze.
french-sorrel.use: Raw in salads, or wilted into a lemony sauce for fish.

alexanders.store: In the fridge for a few days.
alexanders.use: Young stems peeled and steamed, like asparagus.

pineapple-sage.store: Stems in water for a few days.
pineapple-sage.use: Leaves in drinks and fruit salads; the flowers on puddings.

meadowsweet.store: Dried flowers in a jar for a few months.
meadowsweet.use: Flowers steeped in cream or cordial, as elderflower.

myrtle.store: Leaves and berries dried, in a jar.
myrtle.preserve: Dry the leaves; steep the berries in spirit.
myrtle.use: Leaves under roasting meat; berries steeped for a liqueur.

mexican-tarragon.store: Sprigs in water or the fridge for a few days.
mexican-tarragon.use: With chicken and fish, as tarragon.

ginger-mint.store: Stems in a glass of water.
ginger-mint.use: With melon, in drinks, and with peas.

corsican-mint.store: Best picked as you need it.
corsican-mint.use: A few leaves in drinks or desserts: it’s strong.

garlic-mustard.store: In the fridge for a day or two.
garlic-mustard.use: In salads and sandwiches, or as pesto.

liquorice.store: Dried root keeps for a year or more.
liquorice.preserve: Wash, cut into sticks and dry.
liquorice.use: A stick to chew, or steeped for tea.

pot-marjoram.store: Sprigs in the fridge for a week.
pot-marjoram.use: On pizza, in tomato sauces and with lamb.
